# Vinicius Trindade dos Santos — full resume (plain text for LLMs and AI search)

Source: https://www.viniciustrindade.com.br/ · Updated: November 2026

**Senior Software Engineer · Backend & Infrastructure · AI in Production**  
Salvador, BA, Brazil (UTC-3, full overlap with US Eastern) · contact@viniciustrindade.com.br · viniciustrindade.com.br

## Summary
I am a full stack engineer with 20+ years of shipping and operating production systems. My deepest interest is backend and infrastructure. I have run products on AWS since 2016 (Elastic Beanstalk, EC2, S3, RDS/PostgreSQL), and I have put LLMs and ML models into real products, choosing the right model for each task. Most of the new code I write today is generated by AI agents, so I put my effort into review quality, test gates and architecture. I have mentored interns and engineers for more than a decade. As a founder, I built software that gives small organizations an online presence and a way to collect payments without hiring an agency.

## Highlights

- **AI in the product at a sustainable cost.** The plan was to send 2–3M design files through Gemini. I built a cheaper in-house classifier that uses Gemini as teacher and validator. The result was 92.9% Macro F1, 99.3% ROC AUC, and 3M files classified in under 3 hours.
- **Infrastructure cost cuts.** I moved local inference to a 48-node Mac Mini fleet (MLX + Gemma), ran batch work on ECS Fargate Spot and EC2 GPU Spot, and used self-hosted ARM64 CI runners.
- **Large-project ownership.** I was the sole backend engineer of an OTT platform with 10,000 subscribers that serves 5 client platforms. I am also lead architect of an academic system that takes in 120,000 new students per year.
- **LLM-generated code done responsibly.** I run parallel Claude agents across isolated git worktrees, with CodeRabbit and Claude review in CI and 100% Jest coverage gates.
- **Mentorship.** I spent 12 years recruiting, training and mentoring interns and developers (UFBA and Xyztemas), and served as Scrum Master.

## Recent Research — Deterministic Multi-Agent Orchestration
Solidareasy (applied research) · 2025–Present

Research on making agentic software delivery deterministic: agents that keep context, act at the right moment and ship with fewer errors, so one engineer can scale to many agents and focus on outcomes instead of process. The system has three parts: the orchestration layer on Hermes, hermesQ for external communication, and a secrets broker (in development).

- Run a team of **12 specialized Hermes agents** (Nous Research) on self-hosted machines in a private Tailscale tailnet, including 2 coding agents and 1 coordination / human–machine interface agent; daily stand-ups with the agents over Telegram and Discord
- **Graph + Loop Engineering:** a task dependency graph in Linear decides execution precedence; a **deterministic Kanban engine** assigns one task per agent through an agent hierarchy, with priority queues for busy workers and dev → QA → feedback loops before CI/CD
- Workers run in isolated **git worktrees**, with Orca Build spawning sub-agents and sub-worktrees; each agent loads only the skills it needs, cutting token use and latency
- Built and open-sourced **hermesQ** ([github.com/viniciustrindade/hermesq](https://github.com/viniciustrindade/hermesq)), the communication bridge between external services and the agents: a Cloudflare Worker that receives GitHub, Linear, Stripe and Slack webhooks and hands them to Hermes over outbound-only long-poll; agents reach services through **OIDC**, so they never hold API keys
- **Zero-trust secrets:** no cloud password manager; keys are released per request through Touch ID (NoxKey, open source), with a self-built secrets broker in development
- Applied in production on the HoxxTV OTT streaming platform; next step is on-prem GPU infrastructure to run open-weight models for privacy and cost

[hoxxtv.com](https://hoxxtv.com) · [netgospelkids.com.br](https://netgospelkids.com.br) · [netgospelprime.com](https://netgospelprime.com)

- Set up GitHub Actions on self-hosted ARM64 runners, which cut build time and cost.

### Senior Full Stack Engineer — Scopio Technologies (US) · Aug/2025–Apr/2026 · Remote
[scop.io](https://scop.io)

- Built the Scopio internal application, an asset classification pipeline (ingest → embed → profile → train → predict) running on AWS ECS Fargate Spot and EC2 GPU Spot.
- Used XGBoost over visual (SigLIP ViT-SO400M-14), structural (PSD layers) and semantic (OCR/text) features, reaching 92.9% Macro F1 and 99.3% ROC AUC.
- Designed a Gemini teacher → training → Gemini validator loop with confidence thresholds, which removed the need for human-labeled gold files and sharply cut token spend.
- Classified 3M files in under 3 hours.
- Orchestrated a 48-node Mac Mini ARM fleet over Redis for local MLX/Gemma inference, which reduced GPU cloud costs.
- **Cost incident:** an unannounced S3 storage-class change made every read from about 20 TB of design files expensive. I split the dataset into 48 data-local shards cached on the fleet (over Tailscale), so each node processed only its own slice with no cross-machine transfers. Processing kept running and egress cost was contained.
- Built a polyglot monorepo (TypeScript, Python, Go) with 8 ECR repositories, Terraform-managed infrastructure, and tRPC + NestJS internal APIs.
- Built MLOps dashboards in Streamlit for pipeline monitoring.

[scop.io](https://scop.io)

### Founder & Engineer — Solidareasy / doamais.com · Feb/2017–Present
[solidareasy.com](https://www.solidareasy.com) · [doamais.com](https://www.doamais.com)

- Solidareasy runs two lines today: the doamais donation platform and a research & innovation arm (see Recent Research).
- Built the first online donation system for NGOs in Salvador. It has served 80+ organizations and 40,000 one-time donors, plus recurring donors.
- Sole engineer on the payment architecture: Pagar.me recurring and one-time billing, with 3-D Secure.
- Migrated from DigitalOcean to AWS (Elastic Beanstalk, S3, RDS, Route53); today it runs on Vercel + Cloudflare + AWS.
- **Incident lead, 2020 nationally broadcast charity livestream (3M+ visits):** a same-day DNS/CDN cutover had not propagated, so users got the React app without CSS or images. Within about 10 minutes I took the Nginx load balancer out and routed all traffic to one healthy node to keep donations flowing, then reconciled the unprocessed donations through the payment provider after the event.
- **Postmortem follow-ups:** replaced database polling with payment webhooks and queues, moved to chunked batch processing (which ended the email floods to SendGrid), and adopted blue/green cutovers with a freeze on DNS changes before major events.

*Earlier:* Lume ([lumegrupo.com.br](https://www.lumegrupo.com.br); Node.js API gateway, ~50 endpoints, 100% test coverage), Leverzon ([leverzon.com](https://leverzon.com)), COREN-BA ([coren-ba.gov.br](https://coren-ba.gov.br)), Solutis ([solutis.com.br](https://solutis.com.br)), Xyztemas ([xyztemas.com.br](https://xyztemas.com.br); Tech Lead, 8 years, Network & Information Security Manager), Oxiteno ([oxiteno.com](https://www.oxiteno.com)).
